title: FlashAttn-v3 input-shape-aware signaliser and tuning playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: We are seeing intermittent tail latency regressions for a subset of production workloads after the v3 kernel rollout. Root cause appears correlated with unusual input-shape distributions (short+long interleaved sequences, high variance in head counts per request) causing the runtime to pick a v3 microtiling path that is latency-optimal on average but brittle on corner cases. This ticket implements a lightweight 'signaliser' that detects input-shape patterns in real time, runs a small local microbenchmark probe, and routes the request to a safer v2-compatible kernel variant when instability is likely. The goal is to stop client-visible tail latency spikes while gathering deterministic telemetry to guide a broader tuning or kernel change.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Signaliser deployed to canary fleet (5% traffic) and correctly flags >95% of historically-known regression events; 2) Canary shows no >10ms P95 increase on flagged workloads vs baseline; 3) Telemetry dataset produced with sample traces, per-shape kernel decisions, and microbench results; 4) Playbook documenting tuning knobs and escalation path completed and reviewed by RTT/Infra and ML Infra leads.
steps: Define shape signature heuristics (seq_len distribution, head_count variance, batch composition) and thresholds based on historical traces
Implement in-runtime lightweight signaliser with O(1) cheap checks; avoid heavy allocation paths
Add microbench probe that runs a tiny tiled decode (isolated GPU kernel runner) to measure expected latency delta between v2 and v3 for the observed shape
Wire signaliser decision into kernel router with a per-request soft-fallback (prefer safer kernel when probe indicates delta > configured threshold)
Expose decision and probe telemetry to Console (per-route chart) and add alerting for sudden spike in fallback rate
Canary rollout -> monitor -> iterate on heuristics -> expand rollout if stable
experiments: Local perf matrix across representative shapes: {short:16,long:2048,mixed batches} measuring v2/v3 decode latency and memory footprint
Synthetic interleaved-batch test to reproduce the P95 spike in staging cluster using production sample traces
A/B canary: 5% traffic with signaliser enabled vs 5% baseline; collect per-request kernel choice and downstream latency impact
decisions: Do not change v3 kernels in this ticket; focus on routing and observability to mitigate customer impact quickly
Signaliser heuristics will be conservative initially (favor v2 when ambiguity exists) to minimize regressive risk
Microbench probe will be bounded by time budget (<=1ms on fast paths) and run asynchronously when possible; synchronous fallback allowed if probe latency would exceed configured cutoff
Telemetry schema chosen: shape_signature, kernel_choice, probe_latency_ms, probe_delta_ms, request_context_id, route, timestamp
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy signaliser off by default in staging; 2) Enable for small synthetic canary traffic and validate data collection for 48h; 3) Enable on 5% production traffic behind feature flag; monitor P50/P95/P99 and fallback rate dashboards for 72h; 4) If stable, expand to 25% then 100% with rolling 1-hour pauses at each step. Automated rollback: kill feature flag or route all flagged shapes to v2 variant immediately.
rollback_plan: Signaliser toggled off via feature flag. If Canary shows >10% error-rate or >15ms P95 regression attributable to routing, revert routing decisions and disable microprobe. Emergency rollback: pin runtime to commit before signaliser merge using hotpatch procedure documented in runtime-runbook.

2025-02-22 - Liam Chen: Implemented initial signaliser and local microbench harness. Microbench overhead measured ~0.6ms on small batches; need to bound in high-QPS routes.
2025-02-25 - Priya Desai (ML Infra): Reviewed telemetry schema. Requested adding model_id and tokenization-type to traces to correlate with codec-induced shape anomalies.
2025-02-27 - SRE (oncall): Canary alerts for fallback-rate spike were noisy due to sampling; adjusted console chart sampling to deterministic 1:1000 in staging.
2025-03-02 - Liam Chen: Deployed canary (5%) for two internal routes. Observed fallback rate 0.8% and no P95 increase. Submitted PR for review: runtime#8421.

2025-03-04 - Aisha Kumar: Follow-up: add guardrail to avoid probe storms when underlying GPU is saturated; plan to integrate with autoscaling signals in next iteration. Marking for continuous monitoring and further tuning next cycle.
